questions.q: What is a standard object, per this lesson?
options: An object that ships with Salesforce itself, present in every org (e.g. Account, Contact, Case)
An object only large enterprises are allowed to use
An object that must be purchased as an add-on
An object that only exists in sandbox environments
questions.explain: Standard objects like Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Campaign, and Case exist in every Salesforce org from the moment it's created.

questions.q: What is a custom object, per this lesson?
options: An object a specific org's admin or developer built to track something Salesforce doesn't model by default
A renamed version of a standard object
An object that cannot have fields or relationships
An object that never appears in reports
questions.explain: Custom objects behave like standard objects technically, but they're built for one specific company's needs and exist only in that org.

questions.q: How does Salesforce mark a custom object's API name, per this lesson?
options: With a __c suffix
With a leading 'X_' prefix
With all-lowercase letters only
Custom objects have no distinguishing marker at all
questions.explain: The __c suffix is how Salesforce and every tool built on it distinguishes custom objects and fields from standard ones.

questions.q: Why did Chapters 2 and 3 describe objects like Account and Case in general terms that hold true across companies?
options: Because they are standard objects, which Salesforce defines the same way in every org
Because every company customizes them identically
Because those chapters were describing custom objects, not standard ones
Because Account and Case are actually the same object
questions.explain: Standard objects are common ground: Salesforce itself defines their core structure, so descriptions of them generalize across orgs.

questions.q: Why can't an analyst assume a custom object like Equipment_Warranty__c exists or means the same thing in a different company's org?
options: Custom objects are built for one specific org's needs, so their existence and meaning are not guaranteed anywhere else
Custom objects are actually identical across all orgs by Salesforce design
The __c suffix guarantees identical behavior everywhere
Custom objects are deprecated and should never be trusted
questions.explain: A custom object's meaning is whatever the org that built it defined — it has no universal definition the way a standard object does.
